help.title: Help
help.subtitle: How Job Hunter AI works — pages, actions, and the recommended workflow.

sections.title: What this app does
paragraphs: Job Hunter AI helps you discover job openings, score them against your resumes, draft cover letters, track applications, and optionally auto-fill apply forms with Playwright.

Everything runs locally with MySQL. Scrapers pull jobs from company career pages and ATS boards. Scoring and cover letters work without an AI key (deterministic rules); with OPENAI_API_KEY they can use an OpenAI-compatible API.

sections.title: Recommended workflow
paragraphs: Follow this loop the first time you use the app, then repeat whenever you want fresh openings.
bullets: 1. Sign in with the seeded admin account (or your own user after seed).
2. Open Resumes and make sure at least one resume is active — scoring and cover letters need it.
3. Open Sources → Sync from markdown to import company boards, then enable the sources you care about.
4. Click Run on a source (or run enabled sources) to scrape jobs into the Jobs list.
5. In Jobs, review titles, scores, and status. Favorite good fits, reject noise, and create applications for roles you want to pursue.
6. In Applications, generate or edit a cover letter, move the status through the pipeline, and optionally run Auto-apply (fill-only by default).
7. Use Dashboard to watch pipeline metrics (jobs found, favorites, interviews, offers).

sections.title: Dashboard
paragraphs: The Dashboard shows live counts from your database: jobs found, applications, favorites, rejected, interviews, offers, response rate, and high-level technology / country / ATS signals when data exists.

Below the metrics, Focus countries lists your relocation / search priorities by region (Europe, Oceania, North America, South America including Brazil, Asia, Middle East). Chips with a count already have matching jobs in the database.
It is read-only analytics — actions happen on Jobs, Sources, Applications, and Resumes.

sections.title: Sources
paragraphs: Sources are career pages and job boards the app can scrape. Each row has an ATS type, URL, enable toggle, and actions.
bullets: Sync from markdown: imports/updates companies and sources from docs/companies-to-work/.
Enable / disable: only enabled sources are included in batch runs.
Run: scrapes that source now. Supported ATS include Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Gupy, Apinfo, Workday, SmartRecruiters, BambooHR, TeamTailor, Personio, plus CUSTOM HTML fallback.
Telegram / Slack: ingest via source config.messages or bot tokens (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN / SLACK_BOT_TOKEN).
LinkedIn / Indeed / Catho: use export JSON in source.config.jobs (no direct HTML scrape).
If Redis is configured (REDIS_URL), Run can enqueue a background job; otherwise it runs inline. Optional worker: npm run scrape:worker.
History: recent scrape runs show jobs found and status (SUCCESS / PARTIAL / FAILED).

sections.title: Jobs
paragraphs: Jobs is the central list of openings discovered by scrapers or added manually. You can search, filter by status, and act on one or many rows.
bullets: Score: compares the job description to your resume stacks (and preference signals from favorites/rejects). Higher score = better keyword fit.
Favorite / Reject: updates status and feeds preference learning so future scores lean toward what you like.
Create application: starts an application linked to a resume and moves the role into the Applications pipeline.
Enrichment fields (tech, seniority, salary hints) may appear when extraction succeeds.
Near-duplicate postings can be skipped during scrape via semantic similarity.

sections.title: Resumes
paragraphs: Store one or more resumes (e.g. JS/TS vs .NET). Mark which is active for scoring and cover letters.
Content text is used for deterministic matching and as context for AI cover letters when configured. Keep resumes accurate — the app does not invent employers or credentials.

sections.title: Applications
paragraphs: Applications track each role you decided to pursue. Status flows through a controlled pipeline (for example approved → applied → interview → offer, plus reject paths).
Every transition is intentional — use the action buttons rather than editing status by hand.
bullets: Cover letter: generate a draft (template or AI), edit inline, then save. Regenerating creates a new version for that application.
Auto-apply: opens the apply URL with Playwright, fills common fields (name, email, phone, cover letter, resume file when possible), and saves artifacts under storage/artifacts/.
By default PLAYWRIGHT_AUTO_SUBMIT=false — the browser fills the form and returns MANUAL_REQUIRED so you review and submit yourself.
Set PLAYWRIGHT_AUTO_SUBMIT=true only if you intentionally want the app to click Submit (still only marks APPLIED when confirmation is detected).

sections.title: Settings
paragraphs: Account preferences: language (English / pt-BR), theme (light / dark / system), and sign out.

Credential vault: store encrypted Playwright storageState JSON (cookies) for LinkedIn, Indeed, or generic sites so auto-apply can run in a logged-in browser context. Requires ENCRYPTION_KEY in .env. Secrets are never shown again after save.

sections.title: Safety and good defaults
bullets: Keep PLAYWRIGHT_AUTO_SUBMIT=false unless you mean to send live applications.
Never commit .env — secrets (AUTH_SECRET, ENCRYPTION_KEY, API keys, vault data) stay local.
Scrapers respect pacing (SCRAPE_DELAY_MS) and refuse overlapping runs for the same source.
Kenoby and Solides boards are not supported without public APIs; use other ATS or export JSON where available.

sections.title: Optional extras
bullets: OPENAI_API_KEY: richer scoring explanations and AI cover letters; without it, deterministic scoring and templates still work.
REDIS_URL + scrape worker: background scrape queue for longer runs.
npm run eval:scoring: offline check of the scoring policy against fixtures.
Developer docs: docs/GETTING_STARTED.md, docs/SECURITY.md, docs/BACKUP.md, docs/ATS.md.
